Subject: Priv deploy dependency surface mapping for Acme Systems

Hi Alice / Acme Ops team,

Following our pre-sales architecture sync, we'd like to capture a short dependency surface map for the private deployment (VPC + on-prem connectors) so we can finalize the IaC split between Terraform, Helm and Ansible. Goal: identify which resources must be provisioned in your VPC vs the customer-owned on-prem environment, and flag anything that requires cross-team approvals (network ACLs, express routes, IP allocations).

Proposed kickoff outputs (attached in a starter spreadsheet):
- L0 inventory: high-level resources (load balancers, NAT, subnets, routes, peering)
- L1 mapping: which repo/module owns each resource (tf/helm/ansible)
- Gating notes: CI job that must pass before deploy (e.g. terraform plan + unit tests + helm lint)

Ask: can your infra lead confirm IP ranges we should reserve and any change freezes for May 24–28? We want to avoid overlaps with your current subnet plan.

I copied Marissa and Kim — they'll drive repo ownership and CI gating from our side. Vivek will be on-call for any low-level kernel/driver questions during the staging run.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachment: priv-deploy-deps-mapping-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet - starter inventory)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv deploy dependency surface mapping for Acme Systems

Thanks Jonas — attaching a first-pass mapping and a short change set (MR) with suggested module boundaries. Notes:

- Terraform: VPC, subnets, route tables, peering, NGW (customer-owned where they require routing control).
- Helm: platform components that sit in the cluster (kube-controllers, metrics, sidecars).
- Ansible: host-level configuration for any on-prem appliance, NIC tuning, and the install-time secrets bootstrap.

I created a GitLab MR for the split (MR 587). It contains a suggested directory layout that keeps cross-account networking in tf/infra and platform manifests under charts/ (helm). The MR also includes a small orchestration wrapper in /ansible/playbooks/bootstrap.yml to sequence the cluster bootstrapping after TF outputs are available.

Open questions (please reply inline):
1) IP space to reserve (Alice — can you confirm your /16 reservations and whether we should avoid 10.40.0.0/12?)
2) If we use customer NAT gateways, do we need to route egress through your egress appliances?
3) CI gating: propose a pre-merge pipeline that runs terraform validate/plan, helm lint, and a staged deploy to a sandbox cluster owned by Acme.

Attachments: gitlab-mr-587-change-set.diff
Link: https://gitlab.redwood.local/infra/mrs/587

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Infrastructure PM
Redwood Inference

Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks — that layout looks reasonable. Quick answers:

- IP space: we can allocate a contiguous /20 for the Redwood private cluster (suggest 10.128.0.0/20). We cannot change the broader /16 until next quarter, so please avoid 10.0.0.0/8 ranges overlapping our internal reserved ranges.
- Egress: yes, egress must go through our centralized egress appliance for compliance filtering. That means if you expect outbound connections (model downloads, telemetry) they should be NAT'd via our appliance and accounted for in routing.
- Change freeze: we have a maintenance window May 24–25 (limited changes) — after that the team is available for test deploys.

Also, can you provide a short runbook for failover behavior in case the primary private cluster loses connectivity to the egress? We need to confirm behavior for SLA and incident response playbooks.

Alice Chen
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Acme Systems

Subject: Re: Priv deploy dependency surface mapping for Acme Systems

Alice — thanks for the clarity. Attached is a short runbook draft that covers the egress failure modes and our recommended mitigation path:

- Detect: health probes to egress appliance + BGP neighbour session health (if present). Alert severity S1 if both fail.
- Failover option A: route egress through Redwood-managed transit (requires cross-account peering + our transit GW) — will add measurable latency and requires your approval for outbound ACLs.
- Failover option B: graceful degradation: enqueue non-critical telemetry and allow only control-plane outbound flows (model pulls by pinned artifact IDs).
- Rollback: automated terraform destroy is disallowed in prod; we recommend an emergency revert of routing policy via a pre-approved small TF plan signed-off by both parties.

I'm attaching runbook-draft-priv-failover.md and the MR diff that contains the terraform plan snippets that implement the routing fallback. Would Marissa please add CI gating notes to SUP-3421 so ops can track signoffs?

Attachment: runbook-draft-priv-failover.md
Link: JIRA-SUP-3421

Thanks,
Jonas

Quick operational notes — picking up the CI gating / repo split conversation:

- We'll add a required job in the GitLab MR pipeline: tfsec scan -> terraform plan (using a plan-locked state backend) -> helm lint -> helm unit tests -> ansible syntax check. The MR will be blocked until these pass plus a manual approver from Acme's ops team.
- For the routing fallback (Jonas' Option A), we'll need a short cross-account ACL that lists allowed outbound CIDRs and ports. Alice — can your team supply the minimal allowlist? We'll keep the ACL small and default-deny.
- I've attached a draft of the pipeline YAML in the MR (see gitlab link). Also calling out SUP-3421 to track gating artifacts.
